metadata.title: Off-interval spectral convergence for geometrically consistent discrete dipoles
metadata.description: We give an independent proof of the off-interval eigenvalue approximation described in Costabel's OWR43/2022 discrete-dipole question, under an explicit geometric condition: center-selected cubic voxel unions converge in volume to the bounded measurable particle. This includes every bounded Lipschitz particle, for arbitrary grid translations. At every fixed complex frequency, the actual zero-diagonal matrices have no spectral pollution outside the exact static lattice interval, uniform resolvent stability there, and approximation of isolated eigenvalues with algebraic multiplicity, norm-convergent embedded Riesz projections and generalized spectral subspaces. The proof combines Costabel--Dauge--Nedaiasl's established static lattice interval with strong static consistency, Hilbert--Schmidt convergence of the actual sampled dynamic correction and classical compact spectral approximation. A separate compact positive-volume empty-interior support has a nonreal continuum pole at frequency1/10000 while every matrix on the rational meshes is 3x3 zero; its support index is existential. This does not refute convergence for regular particles or establish a necessary geometry condition. Cubic DDA consistency, general spectral principles, continuum pole theory and sphere perturbation are credited prior work. A named 2022/2023 time-harmonic DDA manuscript was not located in the bounded audit, Rahola's full article was unavailable, and a forward-citing thesis was screened only at metadata/abstract level. These priority limitations remain explicit; no first-priority, new general theory or unrestricted compact-support resolution is claimed. The deposit contains an analytical research note and a source/verification archive with original artifacts, exact symbolic/rational controls, illustrative numerical diagnostics and authored adversarial audits. Finite computations supplement rather than replace the proof and do not certify historical priority. AI tools were used extensively in development, derivation, computation, literature research, writing and independent internal adversarial checking. This is an unrefereed preprint without external human peer review or proof-assistant formalization.
